articles.title: U.S. Open 2026: How to watch semifinal matches today, full TV schedule, streaming info and more
articles.summary: The 2026 U.S. Open has reached the round of 16. Here's how to watch all the action.
articles.body:
The 2026 U.S. Open tennis tournament is in full swing. This year is seeing some big names on the court, including Aryna Sabalenka, Elena Rybakina, Jessica Pegula, Coco Gauff, Frances Tiafoe and Ben Shelton. The tournament is airing across ESPN, ESPN2 and ABC. You can stream every match with an ESPN Unlimited subscription.

Here's everything you need to know to watch the 2026 U.S. Open tennis tournament, including the full TV schedule, where to stream matches without cable and more.

TV channel: ESPN, ESPN2, ABC, ESPN Deportes

The U.S. Open singles tournament kicked off on Sunday, Aug. 30, and concludes with the Men's Championship on Sunday, Sept. 13.

The ESPN suite will cover the entirety of the 2026 U.S. Open, with daily coverage of all 16 courts airing across ESPN, ESPN2, ESPN Deportes (Spanish) and streaming on the ESPN App for ESPN Unlimited plan subscribers.

ABC will broadcast all three Sundays of the tournament, including first round coverage, Round of 16 matches and the Men's Championship Preview and Championship.

ESPN Unlimited subscribers will be ale to stream the entirety of the U.S. Open, plus, all Disney+ subscribers can access select Day 1 action directly within the app, even without a bundle subscription to ESPN.

How to watch the 2026 U.S. Open without cable:

Women's Semifinals: 7 p.m. – 11 p.m. (ESPN)

Women's Semifinals (Spanish): 7 p.m. – 11 p.m. (ESPN Deportes)

Women's Doubles Championship: Noon – 2 p.m. (ESPN2)

Men's Semifinal #1: 3 p.m. – 6 p.m. (ESPN)

Men's Semifinals (Spanish): 3 p.m. – 6 p.m. (ESPN Deportes)

Men's Semifinal #2: 7 p.m. – 10 p.m. (ESPN)

Men's Semifinals (Spanish): 7 p.m. – 10 p.m. (ESPN Deportes)

Men's Doubles Championship: Noon – 2 p.m. (ESPN App*)

Women's Championship Pre-Show (Spanish): 3:30 p.m. – 4 p.m. (ESPN Deportes)

Women's Championship: 4 p.m. – 7 p.m. (ESPN)

Women's Championship (Spanish): 4 p.m. – 6:30 p.m. (ESPN Deportes)

Men's Championship Preview: 1 p.m. – 2 p.m. (ABC)

Men's Championship Pre-Show (Spanish): 1:30 p.m. – 2 p.m. (ESPN Deportes)

Men's Championship: 2 p.m. – 5:30 p.m. (ABC)

Men's Championship (Spanish): 2 p.m. – 6 p.m. (ESPN Deportes)

Encore Presentation (Men's Championship): 9 p.m. – Midnight (ESPN2)

*Available on the ESPN App for ESPN Unlimited plan subscribers

articles.title: US Open: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to show the US Open until end of 2030
articles.summary: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to broadcast the US Open; 2026 competition reaches thrilling conclusion at Flushing Meadows this weekend; watch Aryna Sabalenka take on Elena Rybakina in the women's final on Saturday, followed by the men's final on Sunday
articles.body:
As part of the partnership with the United States Tennis Association (USTA), Sky Sports will retain exclusive live coverage of all men's and women's singles, doubles, mixed doubles, juniors and wheelchair competitions throughout the three-week tournament. The agreement was negotiated by the USTA's media rights partner, IMG.

Alongside broadcast rights, fans in the UK and Ireland will also be able to catch up on all the action with clips and highlights available across Sky's digital and social platforms.

This year's coverage has featured augmented reality graphics, enhanced data integrations, in-depth touchscreen analysis and behind-the-scenes content, bringing fans closer to the action than ever before.

Sky's tennis coverage is led by presenter Gigi Salmon and includes expert analysis from Tim Henman and Laura Robson, alongside additional talent and co-commentators at events throughout the season. Match commentary is provided by Jonathan Overend.

The announcement comes amid a drama-filled US Open featuring the shock first-round exit of 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic and the latest finish in tournament history between Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz as the American emerged victorious at 3.33am.

A thrilling women's final meanwhile awaits as World No 1 Aryna Sabalenka takes on World No 2 Elena Rybakina on Saturday.

Jonathan Licht, Chief Executive Officer Sky Sports UK & Ireland, said : "The US Open is one of the highlights of the sporting calendar, featuring the biggest names in both the men's and women's games, all set against the spectacular New York backdrop. We're delighted to extend our partnership with the USTA, reinforcing our shared commitment to embracing innovation, showcasing the best in the sport and delivering world-class coverage for viewers. This renewal further cements Sky Sports' position as the home of sport in the UK and Ireland, offering fans unrivalled breadth and value all year round."

Kirsten Corio, Chief Commercial Officer, USTA: "The US Open and Sky Sports have been trusted partners for many years, and we're excited to continue such a strong relationship with this renewal. Sky shares our commitment to delivering innovative and cutting-edge coverage to a great audience of tennis fans in the U.K. and Ireland, and we're confident that our continued partnership will have a direct impact on tennis' extraordinary growth and deepen fans' connection with the game."

Live tennis is available all year on Sky, including full coverage of the ATP and WTA Tours on Sky Sports or available to stream with NOW and the Sky Sports app. Sky Sports will broadcast over 4,000 matches and 80 tournaments this season.

The partnership extension adds to Sky's already unrivalled portfolio in the UK and Ireland with more top-quality sport than anywhere else, with most sport rights renewed until near the end of the decade. That includes 1,500 games from the Premier League, WSL, EFL and SPFL, exclusive live coverage from every Formula 1 race weekend until the end of 2034, home men's and women's international England cricket, every shot from the golf Majors, year-round coverage of darts, world class boxing from promoters Zuffa and MVP, and more action from the NFL, Netball Super League and rugby league.

The US Open is live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App . You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Los precios de las semifinales del US Open se desploman sin Carlos Alcaraz: ¡19 dólares!
articles.standfirst: El partido entre Zverev y Khachanov no ha despertado ninguna atención en Nueva York
articles.summary: El partido entre Zverev y Khachanov no ha despertado ninguna atención en Nueva York
articles.body: Las primeras consecuencias de la ausencia de Carlos Alcaraz en el cuadro individual masculino del US Open (el murciano cayó derrotado el martes en los cuartos con Ben Shelton) se empiezan a notar este viernes en las semifinales. Las entradas, que inicialmente tenían un precio de 300 dólares, se pueden adquirir en diferentes plataformas por tan sólo 19 dólares. Y es que la primera semifinal entre Alexander Zverev y Karen Khachanov no ha despertado ningún tipo de interés entre el público neoyorquino (antes se había jugado la fina de dobles femeninos) y ha dejado vacía la grada de la central Arthur Ashe, la pista más grande del mundo con capacidad para más de 20.000 espectadores. La ciudad de Nueva York vive de espaldas al tenis este viernes, no en vano se está celebrando el vigésimo quinto aniversario del atentado terrorista contra las Torres Gemelas. La Zona Cero cuenta en la actualidad con dos inmensas fuentes con cascadas artificiales situadas exactamente donde se erigían las torres. Se conmemora la fecha con la lectura pública de los nombres de los fallecidos. Estuvieron expresidentes de los Estados Unidos como Bush, Clinton, Obama y Biden. Faltó el actual, Donald Trump. El último grande del curso empezó poniendo a la venta las entradas más cara en la historia de los Grand Slam. El abono más barato de paseo, sin acceso a los estadios, ascendía a 323 dólares.

images.caption: La pista Arthur Ashe prácticamente vacía.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Taylor Townsend and Katerina Siniakova win women's doubles for career Grand Slam
articles.summary: Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend win the women's doubles at the US Open to complete a historic career doubles Grand Slam.
articles.body:
Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend won the women's doubles at the US Open to complete a historic career doubles Grand Slam as a pairing.

The top seeds came from a set down to beat American wildcards Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7 6-0 6-2 in New York.

Their triumph at Flushing Meadows means they have now won all four Grand Slam titles, adding to their triumphs at Wimbledon in 2024, the Australian Open in 2025 and this year's French Open.

It was Czech player Siniakova's 12th Grand Slam doubles title in total, while she also became the first player to complete the career Slam with two different partners.

The 30-year-old achieved it previously with fellow Czech Barbora Krejcikova.

For American Townsend, who is also 30, victory marks her first US Open doubles title after suffering defeat in the final last year alongside Siniakova to Gabriela Dabrowski and Erin Routliffe.

Siniakova and Townsend had not dropped a set before the final, but lost the opener when the Czech player double-faulted three times in the final game.

They hit back in the second set, winning 23 of 27 points after the first game to force a decider.

Siniakova and Townsend remained in control from there, consolidating an early break in the third set to go 3-1 up before safely seeing out the rest of the match.

Siniakova is one of only eight women to have won at least 12 Grand Slam doubles titles in the Open era.

Should Siniakova end this season as the world number one in doubles, it will mark the sixth time she has achieved the feat, surpassing Martina Navratilova for the most year-end top-ranked finishes in WTA history.

images.caption: Image caption, Taylor Townsend (left) and Katerina Siniakova have won four Grand Slam doubles titles together

articles.title: Townsend, Siniakova win US Open women's doubles title for career Grand Slam
articles.summary: It was a double celebration for Katerina Siniakova and for Taylor Townsend, the final piece of the puzzle to a career Grand Slam.
articles.body:
NEW YORK – It was a double celebration for Katerina Siniakova and for Taylor Townsend, the final piece of the puzzle to a career Grand Slam.

Siniakova and Townsend, the tournament's No. 1 seed, captured their first U.S. Open women's doubles title together, rallying to beat young Americans Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7, 6-0, 6-2 in the final in Arthur Ashe Stadium on on Friday, Sept. 11.

Townsend, a 30 year-old American, and Siniakova, a 30-year-old from Czechia, captured their first major title at Wimbledon in 2024 before adding the 2025 Australian Open, the 2026 French Open and this US Open championship.

Townsend and Siniakova found themselves down 0-3, and went on to lose the first set, but then they turned it on, blanking the wildcard entrants in the second set, before slamming and forehand baselining their way to a 6-2 closing set.

For Siniakova, it was actually the second time she completed career doubles Grand Slam, having already accomplished the feat with Barbora Krejcikova when the pair won the 2022 US Open. She has also won a doubles title at the 2024 French Open with Coco Gauff.

"There was lot of nerves," Siniakova said after the match. "We were really fighting for this one, so I'm just really proud. We did it."

Krueger and Montgomery went on quite a run, beating the defending champions Erin Routliffe and Gabriela Dabrowski in separate matches, as both played with different partners this time around.

It was also a reunion for Krueger and Montgomery, who won the U.S. Open girls' doubles title in 2021.

"I think with what we've just done has been amazing." Montgomery said. "I think we did forget that we were offered a wild card, so I'm just glad we made good use of it, and I'm glad we were able to come back together and continue playing here, especially with our success in juniors."

For Townsend, the match served a greater historical marker for black American tennis players. Addressing the fans inside Ashe following their victory, Townsend pointed out that there were two Black American women competing in the doubles final – herself and Montgomery – on the same day two Black American men will face off in the men's singles semifinals for a place in Sunday's final.

Watch: Townsend and Siniakova celebrate with bottles of bubbly

articles.title: US Open men's semifinals: Score, live updates as Alexander Zverev, Karen Khachanov open play, followed by all-American showdown between Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe
articles.summary: With the final four set, a first-time US Open champion is officially guaranteed.
articles.body: The 2026 US Open continues Friday with two men's semifinal matches that will decide Sunday afternoon's final, the last Grand Slam title of the year.No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev and unseeded Karen Khachanov will open up play, as Zverev bids for a second major title of the season after breaking through at Roland-Garros in June for his first career Grand Slam crown. He steamrolled Netherlands' Botic van de Zandschulp in Wednesday's quarterfinal and will look to carry that momentum into Friday's match against Khachanov, who is still seeking his first career Grand Slam final appearance.The night session brings the match of the day: No. 8 seed Ben Shelton and No. 11 seed Frances Tiafoe in an all-American semifinal at 7 p.m. ET — just the second all-American men's Grand Slam semifinal since 2005. Whoever survives will be one win away from becoming the first American man to claim a major since Andy Roddick in 2003. This evening's match will have a lot to live up to following Wednesday's quarterfinal between Shelton and defending champion Carlos Alcaraz — a grueling four-and-a-half-hour match in which Shelton managed the biggest win of his career as the final shot landed … at 3:33 a.m.Where to watch US Open men's semifinalsAlexander Zverev-Karen Khachanov start time: 3 p.m. ETBen Shelton-Frances Tiafoe start time: No earlier than 7 p.m. ETLocation: Arthur Ashe Stadium | Queens, N.Y.TV channel/live stream: ESPNFollow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest highlights, news and more from the 2026 US Open men's semifinals.

articles.title: Taylor Townsend wins US Open doubles final, praises black 'representation'
articles.summary: Taylor Townsend's victory speech at the US Open women's doubles final sparked debate after she highlighted race and representation at the podium.
articles.body: I'll be honest. I'm fatigued. I'm sick and tired of athletes and media constantly making everything about race. It's incredibly tiresome, divisive, and a massive waste of everyone's time. It's 2026 and we have a Black tennis player, a darn good one, complete the career Grand Slam in women's doubles after a decisive victory, and what does she do at the podium immediately following? She makes it about race. Good grief. Taylor Townsend, who was sponsored by race-baiting civil rights attorney Ben Crump throughout the US Open tournament in New York, alongside her partner Katerina Siniakova (White) defeated former junior champion Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery, 5-7, 6-0, 6-2, in the 2026 US Open women's doubles final to capture their first title in Flushing Meadows as a team. Townsend took to the mic following their victory to grandstand about Black "representation" and taking pride in the color of her skin. Yeah, that's exactly what everyone wants to hear is you talk about your immutable characteristics that don't hinder your ability, assist in your play, or have anything to do with your impressive performance on a court that is literally named after a famous Black tennis player, Arthur Ashe. NAOMI OSAKA 'DOESN'T GIVE A F---' ABOUT US OPEN OUTFIT HATE, SAYS HER HAITIAN 'BLOOD' MAKES HER WHO SHE IS"I take a lot of pride in this: Being a Black woman here," Townsend said in her victory speech. "It's two Black women here in this finals. They're two Black men in the semifinals," she added talking about her opponent Montgomery as well as Tiafoe and Shelton, who face-off Friday night. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Townsend then followed up with, "This is a phenomenal time for tennis, for inspiration, for representation." And there it is. The buzzword she has used over and over and over again at the US Open. In 2025, Townsend, after defeating Mirra Andreeva, said, "I wanna say thank you to everyone who supported me... It’s bigger than me. It’s about the message and representation." Remember, this sports most famous female tennis player is Black (Serena Williams). Again, she's playing on a court named after a Black tennis player. There's no discrimination or lack of acceptance for Black athletes in tennis happening. She's painting herself as some sort of civil right leader and trailblazer, when it just comes across as racially idolatrous. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP In 2024, after the 2024 U.S. Open mixed-doubles final, when Taylor Townsend and Donald Young lost to Sara Errani and Andrea Vavassori, Townsend made it about race saying, "This isn’t the trophy that we wanted. But at the end of the day, I’m the only Black woman left in the tournament. And ultimately, I just hope that Donald and I standing here today, Frances [Tiafoe] in the semifinals, Coco [Gauff] being the defending champion, just shows people that look like us that it’s possible." I guarantee there wasn't a single person watching the tournament wondering if it's possible for a Black tennis player to succeed in a Grand Slam. It's also worth noting that Townsend also hosted the Blacks-only party with Naomi Osaka at the French Open this year.The race card has been overplayed to a nauseating degree. When you constantly play the victim, people don't care to hear it. Now if there was some legitimate injustice happening based on the color of her skin, I'm happy to hear it, but if you're going to lecture about diversity and inclusion in sports, when meritocracy and sportsmanship is what matters most, I don't care to hear it, and neither does the vast majority of the audience.Just play tennis, Townsend. We're over it.

articles.title: Sabalenka vs Rybakina: US Open women’s singles final – start, prize, form
articles.summary: Top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Elena Rybakina clash in a Grand Slam final for the second time this year.
articles.body:
Who : Aryna Sabalenka vs Elena Rybakina What : US Open 2026 women’s singles final Where : Arthur Ashe Stadium, New York, United States When : Saturday, September 12, 4pm local time (20:00 GMT) How to follow: We’ll have all the build-up on Al Jazeera Sport from 1pm local time (17:00 GMT) before our live text commentary stream.

The top two seeds at the US Open 2026 clash in the women’s singles final on Saturday, as two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka takes on soon-to-be world No. 1 Elena Rybakina.

Saturday’s clash at Arthur Ashe Stadium offers top seed Sabalenka the opportunity to complete a rare “three-peat” of US Open titles – a feat achieved by only two other women.

But second seed Rybakina will try to deal Sabalenka another blow, having already ensured the Belarusian’s 99-week reign at the top when the rankings are updated on Monday.

As the pair meet in a Grand Slam final for the third time, Al Jazeera tells you everything you need to know:

Who did Sabalenka and Rybakina beat in the semifinals?

Sabalenka eliminated top-ranked ⁠American Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2 in the first semifinal on Thursday, continuing her bid to join Chris Evert and Serena Williams as the only women to win three straight US Open titles.

In the second semifinal, Rybakina silenced the partisan crowd, rallying from a set down to beat 2023 champion Coco Gauff 3-6, 6-4, 6-4.

When did Sabalenka and Rybakina last meet?

They’ve met three times this year, with Sabalenka winning their semifinal clash in Miami and the final at Indian Wells in southern California.

Rybakina won just once; however, it was the biggest of the three, lifting the Australian Open title in Melbourne.

Rybakina not putting pressure on herself before Sabalenka showdown

Rybakina said she will not put extra pressure on herself ⁠before her maiden US Open final, viewing the showdown as another chance to test herself against a rival who pushes ⁠her to the limit.

“It’s an ‌important match, and since it’s a final, I feel like it doesn’t matter who’s on the other side,” said Rybakina. “I don’t want to put too much pressure on myself, because we’re very close in the rankings.

“Even if something goes wrong in the final, I’ll still have other opportunities and other ⁠tournaments until the end of the year,” the 27-year-old added.

“We push each other ⁠when we play these matches, and you can clearly see what you need to work on more. I think that’s great that you play against someone who pushes you to the limit.”

Sabalenka ready for ‘whatever it takes’ to win

The unstoppable Sabalenka pounded third-seeded Pegula remorselessly with her powerful groundstrokes, saying she was “super desperate” to reach her fourth straight final.

“I wanted it badly to go to the finals, and of course, I want to go all the way,” said Sabalenka, who has had a slow summer since back-to-back wins at Indian Wells and Miami in March.

“The mentality was just I’m ready. I’m ready for whatever it’s going to take to get the win.”

“She [Rybakina] is a big server. She really improved over the years on the baseline game, so it’s going to be a physically and mentally tough match,” the Belarusian added.

The 28-year-old has four major titles in her cabinet: two Australian Open titles (2023 and 2024), and two US Open crowns (2024 and 2025).

The Russian-born Kazakh has two major titles: the 2022 Wimbledon title and the 2026 Australian Open title.

Saturday’s final will be their 18th career meeting, with Sabalenka leading the head-to-head 10-7.

It will also mark the third time they will clash in a Grand Slam final after Rybakina won the 2026 Australian Open and Sabalenka triumphed at the same major in 2023.

History suggests Sabalenka is the favourite at Flushing Meadows, having not been beaten since losing the 2023 final to Gauff.

The current World No. 1 has dropped only one set en route to the title clash, and seems to have hit her peak form just before the final in a “last push of the season”.

That said, Rybakina will be no pushover for Sabalenka. Her fighting spirit and ability to stay cool under pressure headlined her semifinal victory, giving Sabalenka a taste of what to expect as the top seeds clash in a major finale once again.

Rybakina, though, admitted that she needs to step up her game for Saturday’s showdown against Sabalenka, whom she described as an “unbelievable player”.

The last player to win three consecutive titles in New York was tennis legend Serena Williams, the champion from 2012 to 2014.

Former World No. 1 Evert also pulled off three in a row between 1976 and 1978.

The winner of the US Open women’s singles final will take home $5.5m, while the runner-up will be awarded $2.8 million, part of the collective $108m the tournament offered at this year’s edition.

The final will be televised or live-streamed around the world by its international broadcast partners.

You can find your regional broadcaster on the official US Open website’s TV listing .

articles.title: Zverev aspira a un doblete de grandes en Nueva York y atrapa a Sinner como número 1 de la temporada
articles.standfirst: El alemán, primer favorito del cuadro, se impone en la semifinal a Khachanov en tres sets
articles.summary: El alemán, primer favorito del cuadro, se impone en la semifinal a Khachanov en tres sets
articles.body: El cuadro individual masculino del US Open tendrá un nuevo campeón y ya se sabe el primer candidato a revelar a Carlos Alcaraz en el palmarés. Se trata de Alexander Zverev, verdugo de Karen Khachanov, por 6-3, 7-6(7) y 7-6(7). Zverev aspirará este domingo a un doblete de grandes en un mismo curso. Cabe recordar que el pasado mes de junio, estrenó su palmarés de 'majors' en la tierra de Roland Garros. Y que después jugó también la final de Wimbledon. El precio a tanta regularidad es que Sascha, ahora sí, es una amenaza en el ranking ATP para Jannik Sinner y Alcaraz. Iguala ya los 7.950 puntos del italiano en 2026. Y, si se corona el domingo, se situará el numero 1 de la presente temporada. Nadie acumula más victorias (52 de las que 24 son en los grandes) que el tenista natural de Hamburgo. A sus 29 años, ha llegado al punto de plena madurez. El partido con Khachanov, el sexto que disputaba en las pistas de Flushing Meadows, era el primero que jugaba con luz solar y lejos de la sesión nocturna que tanto le gusta para poder dormir más. Las gradas, vacías a primera hora del día cuando se disputó la final femenina de dobles, se fue llenando gracias a los precios populares que se encontraban y que ascendían a tan sólo 19 euros. Entre los asistentes estaban los actores Woody Harrelson y Matthew McConaughey,, y la modelo Camila Alves. Todos disfrutaron de la potencia de Sascha y su estado de confianza. Es por ello que fue capaz de levantar dos pelotas de tercer set, con 6-4 abajo en el 'tie break'. Este espera en la final a un tenista local. Saldrá del duelo que cruzará a los estadounidenses Frances Tiafoe y Ben Shelton. Casi nadie irá con Zverev el domingo aunque ya está acostumbrado a ello.

articles.title: US Open Tennis 2026 Results, Friday's Bracket Winners, Losers and Highlights
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev is headed to another major final.
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev is headed to another major final.

The top seed defeated Karen Khachanov in straight sets to reach his third consecutive Grand Slam final.

On Sunday, Zverev will face either Ben Shelton or Frances Tiafoe in the men's final.

No. 1 Alexander Zverev def. Karen Khachanov, 6-3, 7-6 (7) 7-6 (6)

Karen Khachanov's remarkable run ended on Friday.

Top seed Alexander Zverev stayed dominant, defeating Khachanov in straight sets.

Both players held serve early, but Zverev's relentless defense wore Khachanov down, allowing him to break and take the first set.

Zverev broke again early in the second set, but Khachanov quickly responded, snapping Zverev's streak of 37 consecutive service holds.

Khachanov threatened another break, but Zverev's powerful serve kept him in control.

The set went to a tiebreak, with Zverev pulling ahead before Khachanov fought back with four straight points.

Despite the comeback, Zverev remained composed and edged out the tiebreak 9-7 to claim a two-set lead.

In the third set, both players held serve, leading to another tiebreak. Khachanov surged ahead 5-2 and served for the set at 6-4 but failed to convert, sending forehands long. Zverev then won the final two points to seal the victory.

It was another impressive performance for the 2026 Wimbledon champion, who was consistently hitting first serves around 130 MPH while neutralizing Khachanov's dangerous forehand with top-tier defense.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Alexander Zverev beats Karen Khachanov to reach final
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev beats Karen Khachanov at the US Open to reach a third Grand Slam final in a row and continue his bid for a second major of the year.
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev beat Karen Khachanov at the US Open to reach a third Grand Slam final in a row and continue his bid for a second major of the year.

The top seed put in a commanding performance to beat the Russian 6-3 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (8-6).

Germany's Zverev is the favourite in New York after ending his long wait for a Grand Slam title with his French Open triumph in June.

He reached the Wimbledon final in July, losing in four sets to world number one Jannik Sinner.

The 29-year-old will play either eighth seed Ben Shelton or 11th seed Frances Tiafoe in Sunday's showpiece, with the two Americans set to meet in Friday's night session.

"I think it [Sunday] will be incredibly special especially, these two guys are crowd favourites and everyone loves them," said Zverev.

"Tonight will be an epic semi-final and I am looking forward to watching it. Hopefully I can not make their American dream come true."

With Sinner and defending US Open champion Carlos Alcaraz suffering with injuries this year, Zverev has found a consistency that has allowed him to reach all four Grand Slam semi-finals.

He started off the tournament in New York slowly, being taken to five sets in his opening two matches, but has not dropped a set since.

Zverev faced brief moments of pressure against world number 50 Khachanov, saving two set points in the third set, but otherwise remained in control.

"After the second round, at about 3am I was sitting with my team in the locker room and we were laughing at how bad I was playing," Zverev said.

"That sense of humour helped me. I obviously have improved a bit otherwise I would not be in the US Open final."

Zverev won 13 of 15 points behind his first serve and all nine points at the net in the first set as he broke Khachanov to go 5-3 up before serving out the opener.

Khachanov fought back after going a break down early in the second set and forced a tie-break, saving set point with a magnificent backhand to polish off a 22-shot rally.

In a pivotal point of the match, it was Zverev who took the initiative to earn another set point, converting it as he outlasted Khachanov in a draining rally with some magnificent defence from the baseline.

In the third set, both players remained on serve without conceding a single break point to reach another tie-break.

It was Khachanov who settled quickest into the tie-break, opening up a lead and creating two set points - both of which were saved by Zverev.

From there the top seed never looked back, ultimately clinching victory as Khachanov put a forehand long.

After reaching his sixth major final, Zverev stood arms wide in celebration facing his coaching team, before going to the net to shake hands with Khachanov.

Victory means Zverev is into his second US Open final after suffering a heartbreaking five-set loss to Dominic Thiem in 2020.

articles.title: No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev outlasts Karen Kachenov to book place in US Open final
articles.summary: Men’s No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev might have won in straight sets but opponent Karen Khachanov put up a mighty fight on Friday in the first US Open semifinal at Arthur Ashe Stadium.
articles.body: Men’s No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev might have won in straight sets but opponent Karen Khachanov put up a mighty fight on Friday in the first US Open semifinal at Arthur Ashe Stadium. The 29-year-old defeated Khachanov 6-3, 7-6 (7), 7-6 (6) to book his place in his second career final in Flushing Meadows. The match got off to an easy start for the Zverev. He won the first set decisively 6-3 over Khachanov, as the Russian finished with almost twice the amount of unforced errors as Zverev in the opener. But despite the first set loss, the unseeded 30-year-old maintained his composure, forcing a second set tiebreak with Zverev ultimately prevailing 7-6 (7). It was more of the same in the third set with both players going back and forth, trading games. Up 6-5 in the third set and trying to avoid a tiebreak, Zverev went to complain to the umpire about glare from the sun which drew the ire of the crowd on hand. The German went on to lose the game, prompting the second tiebreak of the match. According to the ESPN broadcast, the glare was coming from the glass on the doors of the suites when they are opened. With the issues with the apparent glare still affecting Zverev, he quickly fell into a 4-1 hole but rebounded to tie it up at 6-6 with a trip to the final on the line. After getting to match point by saving two set points, Zverev put away Khachanov and will now look to avenge his first US Open final loss from 2020. It is also Zverev’s third straight grand slam finals appearance, winning his first career major at Roland Garros in early June. Zverev understood his potential fate for Sunday’s upcoming final with the crowd most likely going to be pulling for the winner No. 8 seed Ben Shelton and No. 11 seed Frances Tiafoe. “I think its going to be incredibly special,” Zverev told ESPN. “Especially these two guys, Frances and Ben, crowd favorites here in New York. Everybody loves them. … Hopefully I can not make the American dream.” He will now await the winner of the second men’s semifinal. Up next: An all-American duel between Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe On a somber day in the United States, two Americans will go head-to-head in the second men’s semifinal: Shelton and Tiafoe. The showdown is one for the history books for a multitude of reasons. Both are looking to advance to their first career grand slam final, with Shelton or Tiafoe becoming the first American to feature in the men’s US Open final since Taylor Fritz did so in 2024. One of them could also be the first US man to win the tournament since Andy Roddick in 2003. The history goes even further with two Black American men are facing each other in a US Open men’s singles semifinal for the first time ever. And no matter who wins, a Black American man will advance to the final for the first time since Arthur Ashe made his last finals appearance there in 1972. The winner will face Zverev in the men’s final on Sunday at 2 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Top seed Zverev holds off Khachanov to reach US Open final
articles.summary: Top seed Alexander Zverev out-gunned Karen Khachanov to reach his third straight Grand Slam final on Friday, rolling into the US Open title match with a stra...
articles.body:
Top seed Alexander Zverev out-gunned Karen Khachanov to reach his third straight Grand Slam final on Friday, rolling into the US Open title match with a straight sets win.

Zverev, who followed up his maiden major at the French Open with a runner-up finish at Wimbledon, saved two set points in the final tiebreaker to close out the 6-3, 7-6 (9/7), 7-6 (8/6) victory.

He'll face the winner of the all-American semi-final between eighth-seeded Ben Shelton and 11th seed Frances Tiafoe in Sunday's championship match.

The German predicted an "absolutely epic" contest between the two Americans, after which he'll be out to thwart the winner's bid to become the first American man in 23 years to lift a Grand Slam trophy.

"Hopefully I can not make the American dream come true on Sunday," said Zverev, who came agonizingly close to the US Open title in 2020 before falling to Dominic Thiem in five sets.

After a somewhat inauspicious start to the tournament, spending nine hours and 26 minutes on court in laborious five-set victories in the first and second rounds, Zverev has steadily upped his game.

He needed two hours and 57 minutes to deny 50th-ranked Khachanov's bid to become the lowest-ranked Grand Slam finalist since number 54 Marcos Baghdatis at the 2006 Australian Open.

But the Russian, who fell to Zverev in the Olympic gold medal match in Tokyo in 2021, put up a spirited challenge in the second and third sets.

"Straight-set win, but anything but straightforward in a way," Zverev said. "He played incredibly well, fought incredibly well."

Unable to make any real headway in the first set, Khachanov fell a quick break down in the second.

The Russian couldn't resist a grin when he snuck a passing shot by Zverev to open the fourth game, and flung his arm into the air in celebration three points later when a forehand winner gave him his first break chance of the match, which he converted when Zverev double faulted.

From there, they went to the tiebreaker, where Khachanov denied Zverev on two set points with thumping forehand and a brilliant backhand down the line before Zverev closed out the set.

Neither player mustered a break point in a tense third set. But when Khachanov took a 6-4 lead in the tiebreaker he surrendered both set points with forehand errors. Zverev came up with his 15th ace and sealed the win on the next point when Khachanov sent a forehand long.

"Second and third set I think it's more than obvious that they could have gone both ways," Zverev said. "I just played a few points better here and there, and I'm happy with the win."

A somber note was struck during the national anthem ceremonies of both the day and night sessions on the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks that brought down the twin towers of the World Trade Center in New York.

Shelton vanquished defending champion and seven-time Grand Slam winner Carlos Alcaraz in an enthralling five-set quarter-final clash that lasted until 3:34 am -- the latest finish in US Open history.

Having notched the biggest win of his career, Shelton is now chasing his first major final.

So is Tiafoe as they duel to have a chance to be the one to end American men's Grand Slam drought, which stretches back to Andy Roddick's 2003 US Open victory.

Shelton leads their head-to-head, but they have split two prior US Open meetings, Shelton winning in the 2023 quarter-finals and Tiafoe turning the tables in the third round the following year.

The women's final is on Saturday, when Kazakhstan's Elena Rybakina will try to thwart Aryna Sabalenka's bid for a third straight title just days after ending the Belarusian's near two-year reign atop the world rankings by reaching the semi-finals.

articles.title: US Open pays tribute on 25th anniversary of 9/11
articles.summary: The US Open pauses to remember the victims of the 9/11 attacks that took place 25 years ago.
articles.body:
The Arthur Ashe Stadium glowed light blue from dusk until dawn as the US Open marked the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks.

American flags were flown at half-mast as New York remembered the 2,977 people who died when hijackers crashed passenger jets into the Twin Towers in Manhattan on that day in 2001.

That year's US Open had concluded just two days earlier, with Lleyton Hewitt winning the men's singles title.

American player James Blake had lost in the second round that year and was in Augusta, Georgia, on Tuesday, 11 September.

But the New York-born future world number four says the day "shattered the guise of safety" felt by Americans and many professional tennis players.

"It was something that I just couldn't believe could happen in the States," Blake told BBC Sport.

"I don't know if we were all naive, or living under the guise of safety and feeling that everything was going to be OK, but it kind of shattered that for a while.

"There was a lot of panic, at every level - whether it be from the highest of highs in the political world to the people on the ground, to everyone around Ground Zero."

Blake, who would later reach two US Open quarter-finals, was in Augusta for a sweat test, having struggled with cramp during the tournament.

His father, though, was still in New York, where he worked. With mobile phone networks overloaded, there was an uncomfortable wait to discover he was safe and well.

Blake was living in Florida at the time, and with planes grounded, took a hire car from Augusta back to Tampa.

His next tournament was in Hong Kong two weeks later, and he admits it was far from easy to board the plane.

"It was definitely scary because I think you get so isolated in tennis," he said.

"You feel like the little bubble you are in, where you are a kind of travelling circus, is normal.

"And then when you realise how restricted travel can be, it wakes you up a little bit to the reality and how quickly things can change.

"It felt like there was a safety net around you. We lived in a bit of a dream world where you are living your dream of playing a sport for a living, and that can all be taken away."

Many domestic sporting events were paused in the aftermath of the attacks, and the Ryder Cup - which had been scheduled to take place at The Belfry in England later that month - was postponed by 12 months.

In Blake's view, the return of competitive sport helped enormously.

"I think that was one of the things that brought the country back," he said.

"Sports were stopped, but when they came back having [then President] George W Bush throwing out the first pitch at a Yankees game - I'm not a Yankees fan, and I can't say I was necessarily a George W Bush fan - I was almost in tears at that moment.

"It was special to have a sitting president [do that]. And it also signified we are back - we are going to have sports, we are going to continue on with our lives.

"The world seemed like it was back on track in a small way."

There is always a ceremony to mark the anniversary when the date falls during the US Open, and there was a moment's silence before both of Friday's men's singles semi-finals.

Before the night session - and the all-American semi-final between Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe - a giant American flag was unfurled on court before R&B artist JoJo sang The Star-Spangled Banner.

"To me it's a really poignant moment," Blake added.

"The 2001 US Open, I remember so well. What would have happened if it happened two or three days earlier, and we were all still there?

"To be perfectly honest, a lot of times I feel playing the national anthem at smaller sporting events is unnecessary.

"But for the US Open, being such an international event and having it around 9/11, I think it is a great moment.
authors: Russell Fuller - Tennis correspondent in New York
